newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Prices up but lag firmer West.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Prices up but lag firmer West.

text.p: Singapore light distillates rose on Tuesday on the back of the huge crude gains overnight, but levels still lagged the western market, traders said.

Naphtha in Asia, weighed down by weak demand, only rose $1.50 per tonne on Tokyo's open-spec forward contract $210.50/$212.50 for first-half October while Singapore naphtha swaps rose by 40 cents per barrel to $22.05/$22.15 for August.
Although September Brent crude has already given up 10 cents per barrel to last trade at $19.35, it had risen by 50 cents overnight.
The rise on the physical gasoline was also marginal with a European major only raising its bid for unleaded 97-octane lifting August 19-23 by 20 cents per barrel to $24.80 fob Singapore.
"The arbitrage to the West must be wide-open by now," said one trader on the difference between the low Singapore price and the firm prices in the U.S. and Europe.
"If you have the right barrels and the right quantity, it would be beautiful," the trader said.
But no fixtures had yet been spotted, traders said.
They said the gasoline market was balanced it would be hard to find high-octane supplies.

State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) re-emerged with a tender to buy 25,000 tonnes of 87 octane 0.15 leaded gasoline for September after cancelling its August tender last week due to an overestimation of demand, an Indian source said.
The new tender which seeks the cargo for delivery to Kandla on the west coast of India between September 23-27, closes August 13 and is valid for a day.
